name: Bahamian Contractors' Association
brand_truth: The construction industry's own voice since 1959: 209 member firms, the 2016 Contractors Act, and the push for the Contractors Board.
buyer: Bahamian contractors, trades, suppliers and developers deciding whether dues are worth it; developers and officials looking for a local firm.

direction.why: A register of firms and an association of builders want order, tables and visible structure; galvanised steel and safety yellow are the building site itself.

big_idea: The member register is the front door: 209 firms, searchable from the first screen, beside 'One voice since 1959'; then the record, a two-tap tier finder and the next event.

images.credit: illustrative photography, replace with your own

first.verdict: revise (5 changes: advocacy block, event photo span, finder rows + preselect, phone header, band crop)

current_site_findings: Hero subtitle misspells the association's own name as 'Assoication', and the hero block appears twice
Own site says founded 1959; ZNS reports 1958
Newest homepage post is from May 2025
Membership dues hidden inside an FAQ accordion
The 209-firm member directory, the association's strongest asset, sits on a separate page as logo tiles mostly reading 'coming soon'
pitch_line: Your register of 209 firms is the most persuasive thing you own; this concept puts it on the first screen and turns dues into a two-tap answer.
assumptions: Founding year 1959 per own site (ZNS says 1958)
Developers under $10M turnover: no published tier, finder says 'ask the office'
Skyfall venue address not published; shown by name only
